definitions.explanation: A punitive measure imposed for violating rules, laws, or norms. Used both for international sanctions between countries and for punishments imposed by organizations or groups.

examples.japanese: {経済|けいざい}{制裁|せいさい}を{発動|はつどう}する。
{国連|こくれん}は{新|あら}たな{制裁|せいさい}を{決議|けつぎ}した。
examples.english: The United Nations passed a resolution on new sanctions.

examples.japanese: ルール{違反|いはん}をした{選手|せんしゅ}にはチームから{厳|きび}しい{制裁|せいさい}が{加|くわ}えられた。
examples.english: The player who violated the rules was given a harsh punishment by the team.

notes:
COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
・{経済|けいざい}{制裁|せいさい} (economic sanctions)
・{制裁|せいさい}を{科|か}す (impose sanctions)
・{制裁|せいさい}を{加|くわ}える (inflict punishment)
・{制裁|せいさい}{措置|そち} (punitive measures)
・{制裁|せいさい}{解除|かいじょ} (lifting of sanctions)

In news reporting, {制裁|せいさい} most commonly refers to international diplomatic or economic sanctions. In everyday usage, it can also mean punishment by an authority figure or organization.
